newsitem.title: POLAND: MCDONNELL MAY SIGN AGREEMENT WITH POLAND.
newsitem.headline: MCDONNELL MAY SIGN AGREEMENT WITH POLAND.

text.p: U.S. aircraft maker McDonnell Douglas Corp may sign an industrial cooperation agreement with Poland before the country decides whether to buy McDonnell fighter jets, a company vice president said on Tuesday.
Last week Hungary signed an agreement with the firm which would help the country pay for potential aircraft shipments in the framework of industrial cooperation projects.

"I would suspect that at some point in time we'll have a (Polish) agreement that's similar...giving additional guidance on what product areas are of interest, the emphasis on investment, export," Bud Mitchell told Reuters on Tuesday.

At a news conference opening the firm's Warsaw office Mitchell said McDonnell would build 50 to 100 of its F-18 Hornet fighters at the Mielec aircraft plant in southern Poland if the government granted it the contract.
The government is expected to invite bids next year.
Lockheed Martin Corp is offering its F-16 fighter, Dassault its Mirage 2000 and a consortium of Saab and British Aerospace Plc the JAS 39 Gripen.
Mitchell declined to give the possible value of the contract but said the firm would offer a full industrial participation agreement promising equal investment in Poland.
Lockheed Martin Corp has said it would provide econonic cooperation worth 100 percent of the value of the contract, which it sees worth up to $1.5 billion.

Mitchell said that in addition to aerospace, McDonnell and companies with which it cooperates such as General Electric and Northrop Grumman could invest in the Polish automotive, medical and agriculture industries, among others.
Poland's armed forces plan to replace about 100 of their old communist-era jet fighters in a move to upgrade them to the standards of NATO, which Warsaw wants to join quickly.
